description: Plays a chord accompaniment from the harmony on an MPX stream, with a choice of voicing, rhythmic figure and accent

params.text: Sets how many notes are sounded in each chord
Chooses whether the chord's root is sounded beneath it
Sets the register of the part, -24 to +24 semitones from middle C
Sets how wide the chord is spread, one, two or three octaves
Chooses the voicing: close, drop two, or open
Chooses how much of the chord is used: the triad, the sevenths, or the extensions
Sets how strongly each chord is voiced to move as little as possible from the one before it, 0 to 100%
Chooses the figure the notes are played in: block, broken upwards, broken downwards, Alberti, or waltz
Sets how much of each step a note fills, 5 to 100%
Chooses which steps are accented: evenly, by the metre, on the downbeat, on the backbeat, offbeat, or pushed
Sets how much louder an accented step is than the rest, 0 to 100%
Moves each note slightly off its exact time, 0 to 100%, so a figure does not sound mechanical
Spreads the notes of a chord over a few milliseconds instead of striking them together
Sets how the level is shared between the chord and the root beneath it, 0 to 100%
Chooses between one held chord and a repeating rhythmic figure
Sets how often a step falls: once a bar, once in two beats, once a beat, or two, three or four a beat

inputs.text: Takes the note stream carrying the harmony to play over

outputs.text: Carries the accompaniment on as an MPX stream

notes: mpx IN takes a note stream from the mpx OUT of another DreamerMPX module, and the module does nothing until one is patched there
mpx OUT carries a note stream, not a voltage; patch it to another DreamerMPX module's mpx IN, or to fromMPX where ordinary voltages are wanted
up to four MPX cables can be patched into the one MPX input, and the notes arriving on them are merged
a cable between two MPX jacks turns pink once it has taken; a cable from an MPX jack to anything else keeps its ordinary colour and carries nothing
there is no clock input here; the beat is read from the MPX stream, so the chart or progression upstream sets the tempo
the chord and the beat both come from the MPX stream patched in, and only mpxChart and mpxProgression put harmony on a stream, so nothing sounds until one of those reaches this input
an MPX cable carries a note stream rather than a voltage and goes to an MPX input; fromMPX turns a stream back into gates and pitch for the wider rack
